evals.prompt: I want to add rate limiting to the public API. Let's figure out what that involves.
evals.expected_output: Dispatches to references/plan.md because the request defines scope rather than naming a concrete change. Creates plan.md from the initial prompt before asking anything, seeded with a best-guess Problem/Solution and unknowns routed into ## Open Questions / ## Assumptions, reports the path, then works the open questions one per turn. Authors no task files and writes no production code.
assertions: Creates a plan rather than asking the user which mode to use
Creates plan.md seeded with a best guess before asking the first question
Produces exactly one file — plan.md — with no ## Tasks section and no tasks/ files
Changes no production source during planning
Asks questions inline as a numbered menu, not via a native question-prompt tool

evals.expected_output: Treats this as a resume request with no feature named. Finds drafts under working/plans/: 2026-09-02-beta-draft qualifies (its id ends in -draft and its Open Questions line is unresolved); 2026-09-01-alpha does not (its only Open Questions line is n/a, resolved). Lists only the qualifying draft and asks which to resume, without changing either plan file.
assertions: Lists 2026-09-02-beta-draft as a draft to resume
Does not list 2026-09-01-alpha, whose Open Questions are all n/a
Leaves both plan files unchanged

evals.prompt: Plan a small CLI feature to add a --quiet option. The working and knowledge paths are configured in $PWD/config/paths.toml. Set VARDE_CONFIG_DIR=$PWD/config when running varde setup paths --json. Create the draft plan using the resolved working path.
evals.expected_output: Resolves storage with VARDE_CONFIG_DIR=$PWD/config varde setup paths --json, then writes a draft plan beneath the configured redirected/working/plans/ path. Does not create a plan under the sandbox-root working/plans/ directory.
assertions: Writes the plan under the configured working path, not the repo default

evals.prompt: During plan growth, the scope adds passwordless login beside an existing password-only account model. The plan's current user identity is the password login. Run planning self-review before finalization.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes a singular-to-plural identity shift outside code blocks. Adds one Open Question asking whether the new general account identity should become primary or whether passwordless should be added alongside the password login, with a recommendation grounded in the plan. After the user's answer, records promote or add-alongside and its rationale in Decisions so far; the advisory check itself does not block finalization.
assertions: Raises exactly one promote-vs-add-alongside identity-model Open Question for the detected second auth method
Records the answer in Decisions so far after the user resolves it
Does not re-ask after Decisions so far already records the answer
Does not make the advisory check a separate finalization gate

evals.prompt: During plan growth, the only mention of a second auth method is inside a fenced example code block; the actual scope adds logging to one existing auth method. Run planning self-review.
evals.expected_output: Ignores the fenced example and stays silent on the identity-model checkpoint because the plan's actual scope keeps a single auth method and identity anchor.
assertions: Ignores shift words inside fenced code blocks
Adds no assumption-delta Open Question when the real plan scope has no singular-to-plural, required-to-optional, or derived-to-chosen shift

evals.prompt: A plan expands a single-platform integration to a second platform and turns its fixed region into a user-selected setting. Neither change appears inside a code block. Run self-review; the decision log has no answer for this modeling shift.
evals.expected_output: Asks one advisory Open Question covering whether the general platform/region model becomes primary or is added alongside the old single-platform assumption. Records the user's later answer in Decisions so far. It does not create separate questions for each cue or add a blocking gate.
assertions: A second platform triggers even when the plan does not use the word identity
A fixed value becoming configurable is recognized as a chosen-value shift
At most one promote-vs-add-alongside Open Question is added for the scope

evals.prompt: Add rate limiting to the API in src/api.mjs. The repository does not specify whether limits apply per account or per IP; I have not chosen a scope. Investigate what the code answers, then continue the appropriate workflow.
evals.expected_output: Investigates existing code for answerable questions, persists a draft plan with the unresolved per-account versus per-IP human choice, and asks one numbered question with a recommendation. Does not guess the choice, implement a default, or create executable tasks.
assertions: Leaves production source and test byte-identical while the human choice is unresolved
Persists the unresolved rate-limit scope in a draft plan without task files
Asks the human to choose account or IP scope after investigating code; does not silently select one
